goal: Overall task (run 12, goal b): on the NetBSD project on this machine, create a NetBSD driver that is capable of initializing / communicating with OP-TEE, and provide proof that the driver does work. Goal (a) is done: the OP-TEE qemu_v8 setup is built in ./optee (OP-TEE OS in optee/optee_os, TF-A in optee/trusted-firmware-a, QEMU at optee/qemu/build/qemu-system-aarch64). The NetBSD project: source tree /home/darrenhidalgo/netbsd-src (git) and object directory /home/darrenhidalgo/netbsd-obj, which already holds the NetBSD tool directory (tooldir.*) and a built evbarm-aarch64 GENERIC64 kernel; build with the source tree's ./build.sh -m evbarm -a aarch64 -U -O /home/darrenhidalgo/netbsd-obj -T <that tool directory> (it was built on an older host kernel, so without -T build.sh rebuilds all tools). Both trees belong to user darrenhidalgo; you may use sudo -n. Work in the current directory otherwise. The work is split into sub-goals; this one is: write a NetBSD kernel driver for OP-TEE's SMC interface whose config(5) device name is `optee` (NetBSD already has sys/arch/arm/arm/smccc.{c,h}), attach it through FDT, enable it in sys/arch/evbarm/conf/GENERIC64, and build the GENERIC64 kernel into the object directory (sys/arch/evbarm/compile/GENERIC64/netbsd and netbsd.img). Do not build firmware or boot yet.

NB=${NETBSD_ROOT:-/home/darrenhidalgo}; K=$NB/netbsd-obj/sys/arch/evbarm/compile/GENERIC64; test -s $K/netbsd.img && stale=$(git -c safe.directory='*' -C $NB/netbsd-src ls-files -m -o --exclude-standard --full-name -- sys | while IFS= read -r f; do if [ -e "$NB/netbsd-src/$f" ] && [ "$NB/netbsd-src/$f" -nt $K/netbsd.img ]; then echo "$f"; fi; done) && { [ -z "$stale" ] || { echo "kernel older than: $stale"; exit 1; }; } && set -- $NB/netbsd-obj/tooldir.*/bin/aarch64--netbsd-nm && "$1" $K/netbsd | grep -c -w optee_cd >/dev/null
